title: ser_json_timedelta must only affect timedelta values, including in inferred (Any) serialization
answers: ser_json_timedelta='float' makes datetimes/dates serialize as numbers with Any type
datetime keys serialized as numbers in dump_json when only timedelta config set
why does to_jsonable_python timedelta_mode change datetime output
inference serializer uses wrong temporal mode for timedelta
body:
Symptom: with only `ser_json_timedelta` set (e.g. 'float'), values serialized by inference (`TypeAdapter(Any)`, `to_jsonable_python`, dict keys) had datetime/date/time output in the timedelta format, not ISO 8601.
Root cause: `SerializationConfig::from_config` / `from_args` in pydantic-core/src/serializers/config.rs folded the deprecated timedelta mode into the single `temporal_mode` field, and infer.rs used that field for every datetime type.
Fix pattern: keep two resolved fields on `SerializationConfig`: `temporal_mode` (only `ser_json_temporal`) and `timedelta_mode` (temporal wins if set, otherwise `ser_json_timedelta`). In pydantic-core/src/serializers/infer.rs, `ObType::Timedelta` branches (`infer_to_python_known`, `infer_serialize_known`, `infer_json_key_known`) must read `state.config.timedelta_mode`, and datetime/date/time branches read `temporal_mode`.
Constraints: covers all three infer paths (python json mode, serde serialize, json keys). Regression test: tests/test_datetime.py::test_ser_json_timedelta_only_applies_to_timedelta_inference.
applies: pydantic-core serializer inference for datetime/date/time/timedelta and the ser_json_timedelta/ser_json_temporal config
